text:
sunil: Heads-up — Prometheus alert firing for gpu-node-87: gpu_xid_error_rate spike (~12/min) but our k8s auto-cordon didn't flip. Seeing intermittent Xid 13/31 logs and one ECC count bump. :eyes:

ops-bot: [Prometheus] ALERT gpu_xid_spike firing on gpu-node-87 — rate=12.3/min. Link: https://prom.example/r/alerts/17892

maria: ack, saw it on the dashboard. Node currently 72% GPU util, mostly low-priority training jobs + a couple of batch evals.

alex: why didn't the auto-cordon trigger? our current health smoothing window is 10m and threshold is 8/min, but we also require persistent cgroup errors for 3 consecutive windows.

sunil: right — the smoothing prevented action. Proposing a more nuanced workflow for Xid/ECC signals:
1) Soft-cordon node (prevent new pods) immediately when Xid rate > 10/min for 2m.
2) Run automated GPU reset attempt: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <index>` (if supported) and collect dmesg + nvml logs.
3) Wait 120s, re-evaluate error rate. If still > 8/min -> hand off to Slurm: mark node DRAIN for low-priority jobs and allow high-priority jobs to finish (graceful).
4) If errors persist after draining jobs, perform hard-evict of remaining pods and add node to quarantine pool for hardware triage.

katie: +1 but add guardrails: only soft-cordon one node per GPU pool per 10m (throttle) and include jitter so we don't cordon many nodes at once during a regional event. Also prefer migrating preemptible jobs to spare capacity instead of immediate eviction. :thumbsup:

devon: For the Slurm handoff we need to ensure job requeue semantics are preserved. Plan: call slurmctld API to set NodeState=drain reason=XID_SPIKE, then run `scontrol requeue` for eligible jobs. We'll add a tag to requeue only low-priority / preemptible partitions.

maria: here's a suggested Prometheus rule snippet for the short-circuit alert (will put in infra/alerts repo):

```
- alert: GPUXidShortSpike
  expr: increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total{job="node-exporter"}[2m]) > 10
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU Xid spike on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```

sunil: And sample k8s ops commands we run in the flow: 
```
# soft cordon
kubectl cordon gpu-node-87
# attempt graceful drain for low-priority pods
kubectl drain gpu-node-87 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=300 --selector="preemptible=true"
# hard drain if needed
kubectl drain gpu-node-87 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30 --force
```

alex: Where does the Slurm call live? Candidate: a small infra webhook service that accepts node health webhooks from Prom and then orchestrates the k8s cordon + slurmctl handoff. Keep it idempotent and transactional (so partial failures retry).

ops-bot: Runbook posted: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/gpu-health-handling — includes triage checklist, hardware tags, and a troubleshooting script. Automated ticket created: OPS-2345 (gpu-node-87).

katie: Also need to consider cost/availability: if cluster GPU capacity is >85% we should NOT evict unless Xid rate > 25/min or host ECC errors increasing. Add an override flag for emergency removal.

devon: I'll open a PR to eng-infra with the webhook + test harness that simulates Xid spikes and validates the 1-node-per-10m throttle. Will run staging tests tonight.

sunil: rollout plan: test in staging tonight, canary to prod pool on Tuesday low-traffic window, full roll next week if stable. I'll update the runbook and add the Prom rule to alerts repo.

maria: small ask — capture nvml logs and push to S3 with node id and timestamp as part of the automation, makes hardware triage faster.

alex: agreed. Also add a metric exposing how many auto-cordons / slurm-drains we've done to monitor false positives.

katie: fine with the flow. one more point: add fallback routing for hosted API — auto-route new inference requests to region-b for models that are compatible while node under investigation.

sunil: noted. I'll include model routing policy in the automation config and a toggle in console. Thanks all. :raised_hands: 

ops-bot: Closing note: scheduled job to run nightly health-check script on quarantined nodes and report back for HW replacement candidates.
